As of April 17, 2026, my wheat is already the main standing crop, and I will build this year from my usual pattern instead of changing too much. I farm 16.1 mu, but with only 2 people at home and some labor going off-farm, I will not spread myself too thin on labor-heavy cotton. I will keep 13.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest income on irrigated land in Quzhou, and I will hold 3.1 mu for cotton. On wheat, I will push for a safe yield first, so I will keep nitrogen a little on the strong side, but not wasteful, and I will use my well water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. On maize, I will follow the wheat harvest immediately and keep no-tillage on the stubble to save time and moisture. On cotton, I will not chase too much area; I will keep a smaller block and manage it carefully, because cotton needs more watching for insects and more hands. My thinking is simple even though I have schooling: first protect yield, second control labor, third keep fertilizer money where it brings a return. If I must err, I will err a little toward enough fertilizer and timely water, because losing yield costs more than carrying a bit of extra input.
